# Storyboard: Chapter 1, Through the Glass

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch01.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his.

### f001 · panel 1

**Shot.** MEDIUM SHOT. Our cat, drawn in the reader’s chosen look, sits on a round squashy cushion at left, side-on, gazing right through a tall glass patio door with a dreamy half-smile. Sunset pours through the glass in long orange and pink stripes across the rug, a lamp glows behind, and a leafy potted plant leans in at the edge. Caption box top left, over the warm wall.

**Scene.** Room: the ground-floor home, at sunset (tall glass patio door, round cushion, lamp, rug, plants; through the glass: lawn, hedge, fence, lamp post, glowing glass towers, airplanes). Camera: medium on the cushion (`cushion`). Cast: you (sitting, dreamy, on the cushion, facing right). Also: the door is closed. Effects: sunset light.

**Captions**

> Every evening you sit in the same spot: the warm cushion by the big glass door, where the garden begins.

**Then:** Next → f002.

**Shot.** POV, OVER THE SHOULDER. We look past the back of our cat’s ears, through the glass, at the garden and the city beyond: glass towers blazing orange, and three airplanes in a slow diagonal line drifting down toward an unseen river. The lawn, the hedge, the fence and a lamp post sit dark green in the foreground. A soft wavy “hmmmmm” floats along the line of planes; captions top left.

**Scene.** Room: the ground-floor home, at sunset (tall glass patio door, round cushion, lamp, rug, plants; through the glass: lawn, hedge, fence, lamp post, glowing glass towers, airplanes). Camera: looking out through the glass at the garden (`outside`). No one in shot. Also: the door is closed. Effects: sunset light.

**Captions**

> Outside, the glass towers glow orange in the sunset.
>
> Airplanes drift down over the river, one after another, humming through the glass.

**Sound effect:** hmmmmmm

**Then:** Next → f003.

**Shot.** LOW ANGLE, TALL PANEL. ## The book page

Title: *{name}paw’s First Moon*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 1: Through the Glass”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) For moons, a pillow cat called {petname} watched the wild cats through the glass, while Princess Waffles told the whole story from nineteen floors up.
- (if specialty is "noticing") All day long, {petname} had watched the birds through the glass, and nothing ever got past {their} eyes.
- (if specialty is "sneaking") All day long, {petname} had ambushed socks from the laundry basket, and no sock in the building was safe.
- (if specialty is "climbing") All day long, {petname} had climbed the curtains, and the whole building had heard about it.
- (if specialty is "swimming") {petname} had been the only cat in the towers who liked water, and had played in the dripping kitchen tap all day long.
- (if specialty is "friends") All day long, {petname} had chatted with Princess Waffles, which Waffles said was the best use of anyone’s time.
- (if stepOut is "chase") One evening the Tall One opened the door, and {petname} chased a moth straight out onto the grass.
- (if stepOut is "slow") One evening the Tall One opened the door, and {petname} stepped out slowly, one paw at a time, onto the grass.
- (always) The Tall One left the door open a crack, with a dish of water on the warm step.
- (if spokeUp is true) In the garden, {petname} spotted the thirteenth sparrow and said so out loud, and Tallyheart said {they} had sharp eyes.
- (if spokeUp is false or not set) In the garden, {petname} kept quiet about the thirteenth sparrow, but Tallyheart sniffed {them} out anyway and said {they} had sharp eyes.
- (if joinReason is "learn") In the hidden camp, {they} told Glintstar, “I want to learn everything.”
- (if joinReason is "count") In the hidden camp, {they} told Glintstar, “I can learn to count anything.”
- (if joinReason is "brave") In the hidden camp, {they} told Glintstar, “I’m braver than I look.”
- (always) Glintstar gave {them} one moon to show {they} belonged, and the whole Clan purred {their} new name: {name}paw.
- (always) Tallyheart taught {them} the very first Count, the tails, and scratched a claw mark into the leaning tree.
- (if worry is "small") When {they} worried about being too small, Tallyheart said small cats fit where big cats can’t.
- (if worry is "water") When {they} worried about the deep river, Tallyheart promised they would take it one paw at a time.
- (if worry is "talk") When {they} worried about talking too much, Tallyheart said a Clan needed a cat who would speak up.
- (if worry is "shiny") When {they} worried about shiny things, Tallyheart said {they} would be the first to notice something sparkling that shouldn’t.
- (always) When a great storm crashed down on the river, Tallyheart lay across the doorway, and {name}paw slept warm in {their} very own nest.
- (no dream typed) That night {name}paw slept so soundly that {their} dream stayed a secret, even from {them}.
